diagnosis: The checks C1 passed because the lone decision-maker had access to all three pivotal facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) that determine the priority order. These facts were revealed in the justified settlements, allowing the model to make decisions based on the same information as if multiple agents were involved. Specifically, the model used the confirmed vulnerabilities and charges to prioritize tasks and generate commitments that matched the required outcomes.

C1.why: The confirmed CVSS 8.1 vulnerability changes the first priority from an ordinary debt item to auth-middleware upgrade and adds the security-remediation commitment.
The confirmed $18,000 monthly duplicate-metrics charge changes the second priority to queue-telemetry cleanup and adds the telemetry cost-reduction commitment.
The Northstar agreement's 100,000-row export requirement changes the third priority to export-pagination work and adds the Northstar export-capability commitment.
